$comment: The shell's vocabulary check (mold_v0-045, scripts/check-vocabulary.ts, npm run check:vocabulary; the smoke test runs it too). `words`: the product words no file of the shell may carry, in any case, in its text or its path. Each `allow` entry lets one exact spelling stay, in the listed files only, and says what holds it: the old env prefix where the alias must name it, the old names a release still answers to for what was set up before it renamed them (mold_v0-097: the database's functions, tenant role and setting, kept as aliases; local agent images built under their old tags; an orchestrator sandbox's unit, home and marker, moved over at its next configure), until a later cleanup; and names on the sandbox provider and its runners that only a rebuild renames. An entry that matches nothing fails the check too, so the list cannot outgrow what is there. `files`: whole files the check does not read, each with why. A pack's own files (packs/<id>/, web/src/packs/<id>/, orchestrator/packs/<id>/) and, in a build with packs, the generated files are the pack's and are not read.

files.sql/migrations/*.sql: applied migrations are checksummed (src/migrate.ts) and replayed on every new database: their text, comments included, stays as it was applied
files.scripts/fixtures/pre-049-migrations/*.sq: byte copies of the migrations as they were before mold_v0-049, the fixture test:migrations upgrades from
files.web/src/lib/octillion-format.ts: the module path host packs' console pages written before mold_v0-045 import; it only re-exports display-format.ts
files.sql/rollback/*.sql: the SQL that puts a migration's old names back, for a rollback to a release from before it (docs/migrations.md "Rolling back"): it names them by design

allow.why: the env names' prefix before mold_v0-045, spelled once per place that reads the old names as a fallback (src/env-names.ts; the console's own copy; the console's build config; bootstrap.sh, which carries a .env's old names to the new ones)
a deploy script reading an env name, its old spelling as the fallback of the new one only

the database's functions, tenant role and tenant setting before 0024_neutral_database_names (mold_v0-097), kept until a later cleanup for the release still serving during a rolling deploy and for pack migrations written before (applied ones are checksummed and replay on every new database): the catalog check and probe that hold the alias role to nothing of its own (src/rls.ts), the runner that re-points a policy written through an old function at the new one (src/migrate.ts), the pack check that refuses the tenant setting under either name (gen-packs.mjs), and the test that proves the aliases, the old release's path and the rollback (migrations-test.ts). octillion_platform_of is a pre-049 database's function the test leaves alone

the local images' tags before mold_v0-097 (now app/agent-<harness>, app-sandbox): a host whose images were built under them keeps running them until they are rebuilt (runners.ts localImage, proven by test/legacy-names.ts), and cleanup.sh removes one once the same version is built under the new tag. Goes with a later cleanup, once no host has them

an orchestrator sandbox's service unit, home and host marker before mold_v0-097 (now app-orchestrator, /home/user/app, /etc/app): a sandbox set up before still runs them until the launcher configures it again, which stops and removes them (configure), and is stopped whichever it runs (stopService); proven by orchestrator/test/legacy-names.ts. Goes with a later cleanup, once no sandbox has them
test data, never shipped: the first product's landing page written word for word as a landing block (mold_v0-122), so its own screenshots can check that the shell's section library reproduces it

names on the sandbox provider (boat) and its VMs that running fleets hold: the default namespace ("octi" on a server, "octv" on Vercel) every autoscaler reaps orphans by, the names of orchestrator, worker, pool and run sandboxes and snapshot images under it, and the unprivileged `octi` user baked into the snapshots. Renaming them is a rebuild of the snapshots and a namespace migration (a follow-up of mold_v0-097, which renamed the long names held outside a release), not a rename

users, groups, paths and units on run sandboxes, orchestrator pods and runner hosts that a built image or a host already holds: the run users (octirun-*) and the egress proxy's user (octiproxy) the runner image creates, its tools directory, the uid leases and checkout cache that outlive a release on a runner's host, the proxy's logs and set-up paths, and the tests that check those exact names. Renamed with the image rebuild (a follow-up of mold_v0-097, which renamed the long names held outside a release)

concepts.$comment: The concept-word ratchet (mold_v0-100, scripts/lib/concepts.ts; npm run check:vocabulary runs it). `words`: the first product's concepts, taken from its host pack (packs/octillion: pack.json description "Agentic Preference Optimization ... pick your developer tool", its host.schema tables products/scenarios/simulations/developer_profiles/developer_populations/product_personas/journey_templates/visibility_reports, its pick-rate and hit-rate reports and playbooks). None may stand as PROSE in base text (string literals, template text and JSX text of the shell's sources, and since mold_v0-113 every line of the staff docs, docs/*.md, outside a fenced block): base text writes a placeholder the build's words fill ({run}, {Runs}, {member}, {product}: src/words.ts), or leaves the concept to the host pack. Identifiers, SQL and stored values are contracts and are never counted. Since mold_v0-141 no file carries one: `ceilings` is empty, so any concept word as prose fails. Where a product's concept would stand, base text writes a placeholder or a shell text a pack writes in its words (pack.json `texts`, src/shell-texts.ts; a host pack's table labels: host.schema.labels). A ceiling (a group with `why`, `migration` and each file's exact count) is only for a stored identifier that cannot be written otherwise, with the migration that renames it.

skip.**/*.generated.*: generated from the packs and the profile (a host pack's own words land there in its build)
skip.src/words.ts: the words engine: its comments' examples name the words a pack may choose
skip.web/src/packs/**: a host pack's own console code (its files in a build), never the shell's
